title_original: Krist Gruijthuijsen appointed director of Stedelijk Museum
excerpt_original: He will succeed Rein Wolfs in July 2027

blocks.caption: Photo: Joel Karppanen. Courtesy Stedelijk Museum, Amsterdam

blocks.text: The Supervisory Board of the Stedelijk Museum, Amsterdam, has appointed Krist Gruijthuijsen as the museum’s new director. He will succeed Rein Wolfs in July 2027.

Gruijthuijsen is joining the Stedelijk from EMMA – Espoo Museum of Modern Art in Finland, where he has been director since 2025 . Alongside his role at EMMA, he is curator at large at Kunsthaus Zürich. Prior to these positions, Gruijthuijsen has served as director of the KW Institute for Contemporary Art, Berlin, from 2016 to 2024; director of Grazer Kunstverein in Graz, Austria, from 2012 to 2016; director of the MA Fine Arts Department at the Sandberg Instituut, Amsterdam, from 2011 to 2016; and co-founded the Kunstverein Amsterdam with Maxine Kopsa in 2009, which he directed until 2012.

‘The museum has long held a special place in my personal and professional life, as it does in the history of modern and contemporary art and design’, said Gruijthuijsen in a statement. ‘Its remarkable collection and rich legacy carry a responsibility that extends far beyond preserving the past. Above all, they call on us to engage with the present and help shape what lies ahead, with art and artists at the heart of everything we do. An essential part of my role will be to deepen the museum’s relationship with Amsterdam: to make it ever more open, engaged, and connected to the city and its communities. I want the Stedelijk not only to reflect the world we live in, but also to actively contribute to shaping its future.’
